title: Progressive Request Trimming & Priority Pipelining for Cross-Region Overload
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a low-latency, graceful overload mechanism that preserves priority for critical traffic across regions by progressively trimming non-essential request work and pipelining early tokens. The feature should integrate with per-tenant priority lanes, model-level circuit-breakers, and regional failover so that latency SLOs are protected even under cross-region degradation.

Background: Current approaches either drop requests wholesale (high user impact) or queue them until capacity returns (latency SLO violations). We need a middle path that: (1) keeps high-priority requests moving, (2) returns useful partial results for lower-priority work, and (3) coordinates with cross-region routing so we don't excessively overcommit remote capacity.

Proposal overview:
- Priority pipelining: classify requests into three runtime lanes (priority, standard, background). For priority lane, allow speculative token streaming and reserve a small fast-path token budget that is guaranteed at admission.
- Progressive trimming: for standard/background lanes, implement an ordered trim pipeline that removes optional request components in stages: 1) drop non-required metadata/attachments, 2) run a fast summarization pre-pass on long prompts to reduce token load, 3) fall back to lower max_tokens / early-stopping logits, 4) if still over budget, return a partial response with a continuation token for later completion.
- Token-budget translation across regions: define a normalized cost unit (NCU) so when routing to another region, we translate local budgets to remote capacity expectations to avoid surprise tail latency.
- Circuit-breaker hooks: extend model circuit-breakers to expose current NCU pressure and per-lane admission hints so the pipeliner can throttle more precisely than a binary open/closed breaker.
- Observability and SLO mapping: surface per-lane latency percentiles, partial-response rates, continuation completion rates, and customer-level NCU consumption in Console dashboards and alerts.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Quality degradation is lossy; acceptance criteria require product signoff for any degraded output modes.
- Continuation tokens introduce complexity for idempotency and billing; we propose using a short-lived continuation token tied to the original request id and billed pro-rata.
- Multi-region translation adds telemetry and config complexity; start with a simple linear NCU multiplier per region and evolve as we measure.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end integration test that shows priority lane 99th latency is under SLO during a 2x traffic surge with regional capacity reduction simulated.
- Partial response mode toggled by feature flag and gated by product review.
- Dashboard panels added for per-lane metrics and continuation success rate.
- Documentation and runbook for on-call describing how to interpret pipeliner signals and when to enable cross-region draining.
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with runtime, routing and Console owners. Agreed on three lanes, preliminary NCU definition.
2025-02-18: Prototype trimming pipeline implemented in staging. Early trimming rules (metadata drop, summarization) applied before tokenization. Observed 25% median token reduction on long prompts.
2025-02-24: Integrated simple NCU translator for us-east->eu-west; found mismatch in tokenization cost assumptions. Updated translation multiplier and reran benchmarks.
2025-03-01: Circuit-breaker team added instrumentation endpoint exposing per-model NCU pressure. Began wiring admission hints into pipeliner.
2025-03-02: Demo to PM and Reliability with simulated region outage. Priority lane kept 99p latency within SLO; standard lane had 18% partial responses — flagged for UX review.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Li): Positive on preserving priority traffic; asked for clearer billing language for continuations and requirement for explicit customer opt-in for lossy modes.
Design (Maya Rivera): Partial-response UX needs failover-aware phrasing and explicit 'continue' affordance; suggested small user-visible indicators when output was trimmed.
Security (Chen Wu): Requested threat model for continuation tokens and recommended short TTL + rotation via KMS.
